edges.description: Loss of functional F12 product lowers circulating factor XII activity and antigen.
The laboratory phenotype is the direct measurement of this plasma state, by coagulant activity and by antigen.
Factor XII is the protease that starts the contact pathway, so its absence prevents surface-triggered initiation of intrinsic coagulation.
The same protease feeds the bradykinin-generating arm of the contact system, so deficiency lowers kallikrein-kinin output as well.
The aPTT reagent works by contact activation, so an assay that depends on factor XII is prolonged in its absence.
Platelet-released polyphosphate is the physiological factor XII activator, so without factor XII that route to fibrin within a growing thrombus is lost. Demonstrated in factor XII-deficient mice.

edges.description: Arterial thrombus formation and stabilisation fail across three vascular beds, and human factor XII restores it.
edges.limitations: Whether human factor XII deficiency confers the same thromboprotection is unresolved: the human evidence is from heterozygous carriers, and complete human deficiency has not been tested for thrombosis protection.

edges.description: Factor XII deficiency occurs naturally and commonly in domestic cats, and none of 26 deficient cats had abnormal bleeding. Residual activity tracked mutation number and type, as in human patients.
edges.limitations: An observational veterinary series rather than a controlled challenge, and the cats were ascertained through laboratory submissions.

nodes.description: The intrinsic (contact) pathway cannot be initiated on a negatively charged surface, so no fibrin forms in the aPTT reaction. This is the whole basis of the laboratory abnormality, and because the pathway is dispensable for hemostasis in vivo it is also the reason the abnormality is harmless.

evidence.reference_title: Factor XII Deficiency and Thrombosis Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.snippet: Factor XII (FXII) initiates the intrinsic coagulation pathway. Despite its role in contact activation assays, FXII deficiency is not associated with bleeding.

meta.association: Biallelic loss-of-function variants, mostly missense with frameshift, deletion and nonsense alleles also reported; the 46C>T promoter polymorphism contributes additively

evidence.snippet: Eight patients with mild FXII deficiency were found to be homozygous for a hypomorphic variant of functional polymorphism C46T and have no other deleterious substitutions in the F12 gene.

nodes.description: Biallelic F12 variants abolish or reduce production of functional factor XII. The spectrum is population-dependent: missense alleles dominate in a Han Chinese cohort, where the abstract reports clustering in the catalytic and kringle domains although its own body describes the variants as spread across the gene, while a Russian cohort is 92.5% promoter and splice variants with no missense predominance. Most variant carriers have a quantitative (type I) defect in which antigen falls with activity; a qualitative (type II) defect with preserved antigen is less common. The common promoter polymorphism 46C>T lowers factor XII levels and contributes additively in many probands.

evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis revealed that 94.1% of probands carried genetic defects, with 29 mutations pinpointed in the F12 gene.

evidence.snippet: We also show that F12 variant carriers generally experience a quantitative (type I) defect in circulating factor XII levels, though a subset of participants was also identified with possible qualitative (type II) deficiency.

nodes.description: During cardiopulmonary bypass the activated clotting time is contact activated and so is already prolonged at baseline, which makes it useless for steering heparin dosing or reversal. Measuring heparin concentration instead, with heparin dose-response and protamine titration, allows bypass to proceed safely.

evidence.snippet: This deficiency is important in the patient undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass because activated clotting times are not helpful in determining proper levels of heparin anticoagulation and its reversal.

evidence.reference_title: Factor XII Deficiency and Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
evidence.snippet: Heparin anticoagulation in patients with factor XII deficiency can be safely carried out with heparin concentration monitoring.

nodes.description: In factor XII-deficient mice, platelet-rich occlusive thrombi fail to form and stabilise across three arterial beds, and the defect is corrected by infusing human factor XII. The same animals bleed normally. Whether human factor XII deficiency confers equivalent protection is not established: heterozygous human carriers are protected from venous thromboembolism in biobank data, but complete human deficiency has never been tested that way.

nodes.description: Factor XII deficiency needs no replacement or prophylaxis, including before surgery. The prolonged aPTT invites plasma transfusion that has no proven benefit, and homozygous patients have come through major operations without hemostatic support. The management decision here is to withhold treatment, not to give it.

evidence.reference_title: An unanticipated prolonged baseline ACT during cardiac surgery due to factor XII deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Patients do not experience a higher risk of surgical bleeding despite a markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time.

evidence.reference_title: Thrombosis-free surgical procedures in severe (Homozygote) factor XII deficiency: report of four additional cases and literature review.
evidence.snippet: In a few patients, the plasma was given prophylactically because of the long partial thromboplastin time.

nodes.description: Circulating factor XII activity and antigen are reduced or absent. This is the measured biochemical state that defines the disease, and the only abnormality in most patients.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and genetic spectrum of factor XII deficiency in the Han population of East China.
evidence.snippet: Surprisingly, all probands with heterozygous, compound heterozygous, or homozygous mutations exhibited severe FXII deficiencies, leading to significantly reduced FXII: C and FXII: Ag levels.

nodes.description: Thrombin generation after injury proceeds through tissue factor and factor VIIa, which factor XII deficiency does not touch. Patients tolerate major surgery without hemostatic support, and factor XII-deficient mice do not bleed spontaneously or excessively after injury. This node is why an alarming aPTT has no hemorrhagic consequence. It carries no inbound causal edge on purpose: the contact-pathway lesion does not reach this route, and that independence is the point.

nodes.description: Isolated, markedly prolonged aPTT with a normal prothrombin time. It corrects on a plasma mixing study, which distinguishes a factor deficiency from an inhibitor such as a lupus anticoagulant. The degree of prolongation does not track factor XII level reliably in unselected patients.

evidence.snippet: The deficiency is usually detected through routine coagulation testing before surgery or during a health check, as it leads to a notable prolongation of the activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT).

nodes.description: Reduced or absent factor XII coagulant activity, with antigen reduced in parallel in the usual quantitative defect. This is the defining laboratory finding.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and genetic spectrum of factor XII deficiency in the Han population of East China.
evidence.snippet: Laboratory tests for all probands revealed significantly prolonged APTT ratios and markedly decreased levels of Factor XII Coagulant Activity (FXII: C) and FXII: Ag.

nodes.description: Factor XIIa also converts prekallikrein to kallikrein, which cleaves high-molecular-weight kininogen to release bradykinin. Deficiency lowers the output of this arm. No deficiency phenotype has been attributed to it; its importance is established from the opposite direction, because excessive factor XII activity causes hereditary angioedema.

evidence.reference_title: Coagulation factor XII in thrombosis and inflammation.
evidence.snippet: In contrast to deficiency in factor XII providing safe thromboprotection, excessive FXII activity is associated with the life-threatening inflammatory disorder hereditary angioedema.
